item.title: Discovering Cryptographic Weaknesses with Claude
item.description:
📝 Frontier Red TeamDiscovering cryptographic weaknesses with ClaudeJul 28, 2026SummaryUsing Claude Mythos Preview, researchers at Anthropic have discovered improved ways to attack cryptographic algorithms (the mathematical methods used to keep online data private). This included several major cryptographic libraries—shared collections of code that are used to encrypt data. Flaws in these widely used cryptographic systems could put billions of users’ data at risk.
🔗 Read more: https://www.anthropic.com/research/discovering-cryptographic-weaknesses

item.title: MCP 2026-07-28 Specification: transport going stateless
item.description:
📝 The highlight of this release is a stateless protocol core - MCP is transforming from a bidirectional stateful protocol into a request/response stateless protocol. MRTR (SEP-2322) enables this scenario over a stateless protocol: the server returns resultType: "input_required" along with the requests it needs answered, and the client retries the original call with the answers attached in inputResponses. With this spec revision, we continued evolving the MCP auth and security posture.
🔗 Read more: https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/

item.title: Now Is the Time to Give LLMs Access to the ACM Digital Library
Scientific computing in the age of agentic AI
item.description:
📝 AI agents are beginning to change that equation. Contributors report that agents significantly accelerated software development and maintenance, in some cases helping small teams take on work that would otherwise have required far more time or specialized engineering support. Overall, these case studies suggest that agents are enabling researchers to spend less time on implementation and more time directing the scientific work.
🔗 Read more: https://openai.com/index/scientific-computing-agentic-ai/
